1.1: A man there has been in the land of Uz--Job his name--and that man has been perfect and upright--both fearing God, and turning aside from evil.
1.2: And there are borne to him seven sons and three daughters,
1.3: and his substance is seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred pairs of oxen, and five hundred she-asses, and a service very abundant; and that man is greater than any of the sons of the east.
1.4: And his sons have gone and made a banquet--the house of each in his day--and have sent and called to their three sisters to eat and to drink with them;
1.5: and it comes to pass, when they have gone round the days of the banquet, that Job does send and sanctify them, and has risen early in the morning, and caused to ascend burnt-offerings--the number of them all--for Job said, `Perhaps my sons have sinned, yet blessed God in their heart.' Thus does Job all the days.
1.6: And the day is, that sons of God come in to station themselves by Jehovah, and there does come also the Adversary in their midst.
1.7: And Jehovah says to the Adversary, `From where do you come?' And the Adversary answers Jehovah and says, `From going to and fro in the land, and from walking up and down on it.'
1.8: And Jehovah says to the Adversary, `Have you set your heart against My servant Job because there is none like him in the land, a man perfect and upright, fearing God, and turning aside from evil?'
1.9: And the Adversary answers Jehovah and says, `For nought is Job fearing God?
1.10: Have not You made a hedge for him, and for his house, and for all that he has--round about?
1.11: The work of his hands You have blessed, and his substance has spread in the land, and yet, put forth, I pray You, Your hand, and strike against anything that he has--if not: to Your face he does bless You!'
1.12: And Jehovah says to the Adversary, `Indeed, all that he has is in your hand, only to him put not forth your hand.' And the Adversary goes out from the presence of Jehovah.
1.13: And the day is, that his sons and his daughters are eating, and drinking wine, in the house of their brother, the first-born.
1.14: And a messenger has come in to Job and says, `The oxen have been plowing, and the she-asses feeding by their sides,
1.15: and Sheba does fall, and take them, and the young men they have smitten by the mouth of the sword, and I am escaped--only I alone--to declare it to you.'
1.16: While this one is speaking another also has come and says, `Fire of God has fallen from the heavens, and burns among the flock, and among the young men, and consumes them, and I am escaped--only I alone--to declare it to you.'
1.17: While this one is speaking another also has come and says, `Chaldeans made three heads, and rush on the camels, and take them, and the young men they have smitten by the mouth of the sword, and I am escaped--only I alone--to declare it to you.'
1.18: While this one is speaking another also has come and says, `Your sons and your daughters are eating, and drinking wine, in the house of their brother, the first-born.
1.19: And indeed, a great wind has come from over the wilderness, and strikes against the four corners of the house, and it falls on the young men, and they are dead, and I am escaped--only I alone--to declare it to you.'
1.20: And Job rises, and rends his robe, and shaves his head, and falls to the earth, and does obeisance,
1.21: and he says, `Naked came I forth from the womb of my mother, and naked I turn back there: Jehovah has given and Jehovah has taken: let the name of Jehovah be blessed.'
1.22: In all this Job has not sinned, nor given folly to God.

2.1: And the day is, that sons of God come in to station themselves by Jehovah, and there does come also the Adversary in their midst to station himself by Jehovah.
2.2: And Jehovah says to the Adversary, `From where did you come?' And the Adversary answers Jehovah and says, `From going to and fro in the land, and from walking up and down in it.'
2.3: And Jehovah says to the Adversary, `Have you set your heart to My servant Job because there is none like him in the land, a man perfect and upright, fearing God and turning aside from evil? and still he is keeping hold on his integrity, and you do move Me against him to swallow him up for nought!'
2.4: And the Adversary answers Jehovah and says, `A skin for a skin, and all that a man has he does give for his life.
2.5: Yet, put forth, I pray You, Your hand, and strike to his bone and to his flesh--if not: to Your face he does bless You!'
2.6: And Jehovah says to the Adversary, `Indeed, he is in your hand; only his life take care of.'
2.7: And the Adversary goes forth from the presence of Jehovah, and smites Job with a sore ulcer from the sole of his foot to his crown.
2.8: And he takes to him a potsherd to scrape himself with it, and he is sitting in the midst of the ashes.
2.9: And his wife says to him, `Still you are keeping hold on your integrity: bless God and die.'
2.10: And he says to her, `As one of the foolish women speaks, you speak; yes, the good we receive from God, and the evil we do not receive.' In all this Job has not sinned with his lips.
2.11: And three of the friends of Job hear of all this evil that has come upon him, and they come in each from his place--Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite--and they are met together to come in to bemoan him, and to comfort him;
2.12: and they lift up their eyes from afar and have not discerned him, and they lift up their voice and weep, and rend each his robe, and sprinkle dust on their heads--heavenward.
2.13: And they sit with him on the earth seven days and seven nights, and there is none speaking to him a word when they have seen that the pain has been very great.

3.1: After this has Job opened his mouth, and reviles his day.
3.3: Let the day perish in which I am born, And the night that has said: `A man-child has been conceived.'
3.4: That day--let it be darkness, Let not God require it from above, Nor let light shine upon it.
3.5: Let darkness and death-shade redeem it, Let a cloud tabernacle upon it, Let them terrify it as the most bitter of days.
3.6: That night--let thick darkness take it, Let it not be united to days of the year, Into the number of months let it not come.
3.7: Indeed! that night--let it be gloomy, Let no singing come into it.
3.8: Let the cursers of day mark it, Who are ready to wake up Leviathan.
3.9: Let the stars of its twilight be dark, Let it wait for light, and there is none, And let it not look on the eyelids of the dawn.
3.10: Because it has not shut the doors Of the womb that was mine! And hide misery from my eyes.
3.11: Why from the womb do I not die? From the belly I have come forth and gasp!
3.12: Wherefore have knees been before me? And what are breasts, that I suck?
3.13: For now, I have lain down, and am quiet, I have slept--then there is rest to me,
3.14: With kings and counsellors of earth, These building wastes for themselves.
3.15: Or with princes--they have gold, They are filling their houses with silver.
3.16: (Or as a hidden abortion I am not, As infants--they have not seen light.)
3.17: There the wicked have ceased troubling, And there rest do the wearied in power.
3.18: Together prisoners have been at ease, They have not heard the voice of an exactor,
3.19: Small and great are there the same. And a servant is free from his lord.
3.20: Why gives He to the miserable light, and life to the bitter soul?
3.21: Who are waiting for death, and it is not, And they seek it above hid treasures.
3.22: Who are glad--to joy, They rejoice when they find a grave.
3.23: To a man whose way has been hidden, And whom God does shut up?
3.24: For before my food, my sighing comes, And poured out as waters are my roarings.
3.25: For a fear I feared and it meets me, And what I was afraid of does come to me.
3.26: I was not safe--nor was I quiet--Nor was I at rest--and trouble comes!

4.1: And Eliphaz the Temanite answers and says: --
4.2: Has one tried a word with you? --You are weary! And to keep in words who is able?
4.3: Indeed, you have instructed many, And feeble hands you make strong.
4.4: The stumbling one do your words raise up, And bowing knees you do strengthen.
4.5: But now, it comes in to you, And you are weary; It strikes to you, and you are troubled.
4.6: Is not your reverence your confidence? Your hope--the perfection of your ways?
4.7: Remember, I pray you, Who, being innocent, has perished? And where have the upright been cut off?
4.8: As I have seen--ploughers of iniquity, And sowers of misery, reap it!
4.9: From the breath of God they perish, And from the spirit of His anger consumed.
4.10: The roaring of a lion, And the voice of a fierce lion, And teeth of young lions have been broken.
4.11: An old lion is perishing without prey, And the whelps of the lioness do separate.
4.12: And to me a thing is secretly brought, And receive does my ear a little of it.
4.13: In thoughts from visions of the night, In the falling of deep sleep on men,
4.14: Fear has met me, and trembling, And the multitude of my bones caused to fear.
4.15: And a spirit before my face does pass, Stand up does the hair of my flesh;
4.16: It stands, and I discern not its aspect, A similitude is over-against my eyes, Silence! and a voice I hear:
4.17: `Is mortal man than God more righteous? Than his Maker is a man cleaner?
4.18: Indeed, in His servants He puts no credence, Nor in His messengers sets praise.'
4.19: Also--the inhabitants of houses of clay, (Whose foundation is in the dust, They bruise them before a moth.)
4.20: From morning to evening are beaten down, Without any regarding, for ever they perish.
4.21: Has not their excellency been removed with them? They die, and not in wisdom!

5.1: Pray, call, is there any to answer you? And to which of the holy ones do you turn?
5.2: For provocation slays the perverse, And envy puts to death the simple,
5.3: I--I have seen the perverse taking root, And I mark his habitation straightway,
5.4: Far are his sons from safety, And they are bruised in the gate, And there is no deliverer.
5.5: Whose harvest the hungry does eat, And even from the thorns takes it, And the designing swallowed their wealth.
5.6: For sorrow comes not forth from the dust, Nor from the ground springs up misery.
5.7: For man to misery is born, And the sparks go high to fly.
5.8: Yet I--I inquire for God, And for God I give my word,
5.9: Doing great things, and there is no searching. Wonderful, till there is no numbering.
5.10: Who is giving rain on the face of the land, And is sending waters on the out-places.
5.11: To set the low on a high place, And the mourners have been high in safety.
5.12: Making void thoughts of the subtile, And their hands do not execute wisdom.
5.13: Capturing the wise in their subtilty, And the counsel of wrestling ones was hastened,
5.14: By day they meet darkness, And as night--they grope at noon.
5.15: And He saves the wasted from their mouth, And from a strong hand the needy,
5.16: And there is hope to the poor, And perverseness has shut her mouth.
5.17: Indeed, the happiness of mortal man, God does reprove him: And the chastisement of the Mighty despise not,
5.18: For He does pain, and He binds up, He smites, and His hands heal.
5.19: In six distresses He delivers you, And in seven evil strikes not on you.
5.20: In famine He has redeemed you from death, And in battle from the hands of the sword.
5.21: When the tongue scourges you are hid, And you are not afraid of destruction, When it comes.
5.22: At destruction and at hunger you mock, And of the beast of the earth, You are not afraid.
5.23: (For with sons of the field is your covenant, And the beast of the field Has been at peace with you.)
5.24: And you have known that your tent is peace, And inspected your habitation, and err not,
5.25: And have known that numerous is Your seed, And your offspring as the herb of the earth;
5.26: You come in full age to the grave, As the going up of a stalk in its season.
5.27: Indeed, this--we searched it out--it is right, hearken; And you, know for yourself!

6.2: O that my provocation were thoroughly weighed, And my calamity in balances They would lift up together!
6.3: For now, than the sands of the sea it is heavier, Therefore my words have been rash.
6.4: For arrows of the Mighty are with me, Whose poison is drinking up my spirit. Terrors of God array themselves for me!
6.5: Brays a wild ass over tender grass? Lows an ox over his provender?
6.6: Eaten is an insipid thing without salt? Is there sense in the drivel of dreams?
6.7: My soul is refusing to touch! They are as my sickening food.
6.8: O that my request may come, That God may grant my hope!
6.9: That God would please--and bruise me, Loose His hand and cut me off!
6.10: And yet it is my comfort, (And I exult in pain--He does not spare,) That I have not hidden The sayings of the Holy One.
6.11: What is my power that I should hope? And what my end That I should prolong my life?
6.12: Is my strength the strength of stones? Is my flesh brazen?
6.13: Is not my help with me, And substance driven from me?
6.14: To a despiser of his friends is shame, And the fear of the Mighty he forsakes.
6.15: My brethren have deceived as a brook, As a stream of brooks they pass away.
6.16: That are black because of ice, By them does snow hide itself.
6.17: By the time they are warm they have been cut off, By its being hot they have been Extinguished from their place.
6.18: Turn aside do the paths of their way, They ascend into emptiness, and are lost.
6.19: Passengers of Tema looked expectingly, Travellers of Sheba hoped for them.
6.20: They were ashamed that one has trusted, They have come to it and are confounded.
6.21: Surely now you have become the same! You see a downfall, and are afraid.
6.22: Is it because I said, Give to me? And, By your power bribe for me?
6.23: And, Deliver me from the hand of an adversary? And, From the hand of terrible ones ransom me?
6.24: Show me, and I--I keep silent, And what I have erred, let me understand.
6.25: How powerful have been upright sayings, And what does reproof from you reprove?
6.26: For reproof--do you reckon words? And for wind--sayings of the desperate.
6.27: Anger on the fatherless you cause to fall, And are strange to your friend.
6.28: And, now, please, look upon me, Even to your face do I lie?
6.29: Turn back, I pray you, let it not be perverseness, Yes, turn back again--my righteousness is in it.
6.30: Is there in my tongue perverseness? Discerns not my palate desirable things?

7.1: Is there not a warfare to man on earth? And as the days of an hireling his days?
7.2: As a servant desires the shadow, And as a hireling expects his wage,
7.3: So I have been caused to inherit months of vanity, And nights of misery they numbered to me.
7.4: If I lay down then I said, `When do I rise!' And evening has been measured, And I have been full of tossings till dawn.
7.5: Clothed has been my flesh with worms, And a clod of dust, My skin has been shrivelled and is loathsome,
7.6: My days swifter than a weaving machine, And they are consumed without hope.
7.7: Remember You that my life is a breath, My eye turns not back to see good.
7.8: The eye of my beholder beholds me not. Your eyes are upon me--and I am not.
7.9: Consumed has been a cloud, and it goes, So he who is going down to Sheol comes not up.
7.10: He turns not again to his house, Nor does his place discern him again.
7.11: Also I--I withhold not my mouth--I speak in the distress of my spirit, I talk in the bitterness of my soul.
7.12: A sea- monster am I, or a dragon, That you set over me a guard?
7.13: When I said, `My bed does comfort me,' He takes away in my talking my couch.
7.14: And you have affrighted me with dreams, And from visions you terrify me,
7.15: And my soul chooses strangling, Death rather than my bones.
7.16: I have wasted away--not to the age do I live. Cease from me, for my days are vanity.
7.17: What is man that You do magnify him? And that You set to him Your heart?
7.18: And inspect him in the mornings, In the evenings do try him?
7.19: How long do You not look from me? You do not desist till I swallow my spittle.
7.20: I have sinned, what do I to You, O watcher of man? Why have You set me for a mark to You, And I am for a burden to myself--and what?
7.21: You do not take away my transgression, And cause to pass away my iniquity, Because now, for dust I lie down: And You have sought me--and I am not!

8.1: And Bildad the Shuhite answers and says: --
8.2: Till when do you speak these things? And a strong wind--sayings of your mouth?
8.3: Does God pervert judgment? And does the Mighty One pervert justice?
8.4: If your sons have sinned before Him, And He does send them away, By the hand of their transgression,
8.5: If you do seek early to God, And to the Mighty make supplication,
8.6: If pure and upright you are, Surely now He wakes for you, And has completed The habitation of your righteousness.
8.7: And your beginning has been small, And your latter end is very great.
8.8: For, ask I pray you of a former generation, And prepare to a search of their fathers,
8.9: (For of yesterday we are, and we know not, For a shadow are our days on earth.)
8.10: Do they not show you--speak to you, And from their heart bring forth words?
8.11: `Does a rush wise without mire? A reed increase without water?
8.12: While it is in its budding--uncropped, Even before any herb it withers.
8.13: So are the paths of all forgetting God, And the hope of the profane does perish,
8.14: Whose confidence is loathsome, And the house of a spider his trust.
8.15: He leans on his house--and it stands not: He takes hold on it--and it abides not.
8.16: Green he is before the sun, And over his garden his branch goes out.
8.17: By a heap his roots are wrapped, A house of stones he looks for.
8.18: If one does destroy him from his place, Then it has feigned concerning him, I have not seen you!
8.19: Indeed, this is the joy of his way, And from the dust others spring up.'
8.20: Indeed, God does not reject the perfect, Nor takes hold on the hand of evil doers.
8.21: While he fills with laughter your mouth, And your lips with shouting,
8.22: Those hating you do put on shame, And the tent of the wicked is not!

9.2: Truly I have known that it is so, And what--is man righteous with God?
9.3: If he delight to strive with Him--He does not answer him one of a thousand.
9.4: Wise in heart and strong in power--Who has hardened toward Him and is at peace?
9.5: Who is removing mountains, And they have not known, Who has overturned them in His anger.
9.6: Who is shaking earth from its place, And its pillars move themselves.
9.7: Who is speaking to the sun, and it rises not, And the stars He seals up.
9.8: Stretching out the heavens by Himself, And treading on the heights of the sea,
9.9: Making Osh, Kesil, and Kimah, And the inner chambers of the south.
9.10: Doing great things till there is no searching, And wonderful, till there is no numbering.
9.11: Indeed, He goes over by me, and I see not, And He passes on, and I attend not to it.
9.12: Indeed, He snatches away, who brings it back? Who says to Him, `What do You?'
9.13: God does not turn back His anger, Under Him bowed have proud helpers.
9.14: How much less do I--I answer Him? Choose out my words with Him?
9.15: Whom, though I were righteous, I answer not, For my judgment I make supplication.
9.16: Though I had called and He answers me, I do not believe that He gives ear to my voice.
9.17: Because with a tempest He bruises me, And has multiplied my wounds for nought.
9.18: He permits me not to refresh my spirit, But fills me with bitter things.
9.19: If of power, indeed, the Strong One; And if of judgment--who does convene me?
9.20: If I be righteous, My mouth does declare me wicked, Perfect I am! --it declares me perverse.
9.21: Perfect I am! --I know not my soul, I despise my life.
9.22: It is the same thing, therefore I said, `The perfect and the wicked He is consuming.'
9.23: If a scourge does put to death suddenly, At the trial of the innocent He laughs.
9.24: Earth has been given Into the hand of the wicked one. The face of its judges he covers, If not--where, who is he?
9.25: My days have been swifter than a runner, They have fled, they have not seen good,
9.26: They have passed on with ships of reed, As an eagle darts on food.
9.27: Though I say, `I forget my talking, I forsake my corner, and I brighten up!'
9.28: I have been afraid of all my griefs, I have known that You do not acquit me.
9.29: I--I am become wicked; why is this? In vain I labour.
9.30: If I have washed myself with snow-water, And purified with soap my hands,
9.31: Then in corruption You do dip me, And my garments have abominated me.
9.32: But if a man like myself--I answer him, We come together into judgment.
9.33: If there were between us an umpire, He does place his hand on us both.
9.34: He does turn aside from off me his rod, And His terror does not make me afraid,
9.35: I speak, and do not fear Him, But I am not right with myself.

10.1: My soul has been weary of my life, I leave off my talking to myself, I speak in the bitterness of my soul.
10.2: I say to God, `Do not condemn me, Let me know why You do strive with me.
10.3: Is it good for You that You do oppress? That You despise the labour of Your hands, And on the counsel of the wicked have shone?
10.4: Eyes of flesh have You? As man sees--see You?
10.5: As the days of man are Your days? Your years as the days of a man?
10.6: That You inquire for my iniquity, And for my sin seek?
10.7: For You know that I am not wicked, And there is no deliverer from Your hand.
10.8: Your hands have taken pains about me, And they make me together round about, And You swallow me up!
10.9: Remember, I pray You, That as clay You have made me, And to dust You do bring me back.
10.10: Do You not as milk pour me out? And as cheese curdle me?
10.11: Skin and flesh You do put on me, And with bones and sinews do fence me.
10.12: Life and kindness You have done with me. And Your inspection has preserved my spirit.
10.13: And these You have laid up in Your heart, I have known that this is with You.
10.14: If I sinned, then You have observed me, And from my iniquity do not acquit me,
10.15: If I have done wickedly--woe to me, And righteously--I lift not up my head, Full of shame--then see my affliction,
10.16: And it rises--as a lion You hunt me. And You turn back--You show Yourself wonderful in me.
10.17: You renew Your witnesses against me, And do multiply Your anger with me, Changes and warfare are with me.
10.18: And why from the womb Have You brought me forth? I expire, and the eye does not see me.
10.19: As I had not been, I am, From the belly to the grave I am brought,
10.20: Are not my days few? Cease then, and put from me, And I brighten up a little,
10.21: Before I go, and return not, To a land of darkness and death-shade,
10.22: A land of obscurity as thick darkness, Death-shade--and no order, And the shining is as thick darkness.'

11.1: And Zophar the Naamathite answers and says: --
11.2: Is a multitude of words not answered? And is a man of lips justified?
11.3: Your devices make men keep silent, You scorn, and none is causing blushing!
11.4: And you say, `Pure is my discourse, And clean I have been in Your eyes.'
11.5: And yet, O that God had spoken! And does open His lips with you.
11.6: And declare to you secrets of wisdom, For counsel has foldings. And know you that God forgets for you, Some of your iniquity.
11.7: By searching do you find out God? To perfection find out the Mighty One?
11.8: Heights of the heavens! --what do you? Deeper than Sheol! --what do you know?
11.9: Longer than earth is its measure, And broader than the sea.
11.10: If He pass on, and shut up, and assemble, Who then do reverse it?
11.11: For he has known men of vanity, And He sees iniquity, And one does not consider it!
11.12: And empty man is bold, And the colt of a wild ass man is born.
11.13: If you--you have prepared your heart, And have spread out to Him your hands,
11.14: If iniquity is in your hand, put it far off, And let not perverseness dwell in your tents.
11.15: For then you lift up your face from blemish, And you have been firm, and fear not.
11.16: For you do forget misery, As waters passed away you remember.
11.17: And above the noon does age rise, You fly--as the morning you are.
11.18: And you have trusted because their is hope, And searched--in confidence you lie down,
11.19: And you have rested, And none is causing trembling, And many have entreated your face;
11.20: And the eyes of the wicked are consumed, And refuge has perished from them, And their hope is a breathing out of soul!

12.2: Truly--you are the people, And with you does wisdom die.
12.3: I also have a heart like you, I am not fallen more than you, And with whom is there not like these?
12.4: A laughter to his friend I am: `He calls to God, and He answers him,' A laughter is the perfect righteous one.
12.5: A torch--despised in the thoughts of the secure Is prepared for those sliding with the feet.
12.6: At peace are the tents of spoilers, And those provoking God have confidence, He into whose hand God has brought.
12.7: And yet, ask, I pray you, One of the beasts, and it does show you, And a fowl of the heavens, And it does declare to you.
12.8: Or talk to the earth, and it shows you, And fishes of the sea recount to you:
12.9: `Who has not known in all these, That the hand of Jehovah has done this?
12.10: In whose hand is the breath of every living thing, And the spirit of all flesh of man.'
12.11: Does not the ear try words? And the palate taste food for itself?
12.12: With the very aged is wisdom, And with length of days understanding.
12.13: With Him are wisdom and might, To him are counsel and understanding.
12.14: Indeed, He breaks down, and it is not built up, He shuts against a man, And it is not opened.
12.15: Indeed, He keeps in the waters, and they are dried up, And he sends them forth, And they overturn the land.
12.16: With Him are strength and wisdom, His the deceived and deceiver.
12.17: Causing counsellors to go away a spoil, And judges He makes foolish.
12.18: The bands of kings He has opened, And He binds a girdle on their loins.
12.19: Causing ministers to go away a spoil And strong ones He overthrows.
12.20: Turning aside the lip of the stedfast, And the reason of the aged He takes away.
12.21: Pouring contempt upon princes, And the girdle of the mighty He made feeble.
12.22: Removing deep things out of darkness, And He brings out to light death-shade.
12.23: Magnifying the nations, and He destroys them, Spreading out the nations, and He quiets them.
12.24: Turning aside the heart Of the heads of the people of the land, And he causes them to wander In vacancy--no way!
12.25: They feel darkness, and not light, He causes them to wander as a drunkard.

13.1: Indeed, all--has my eye seen, Heard has my ear, and it attends to it.
13.2: According to your knowledge I have known--also I. I am not fallen more than you.
13.3: Yet I for the Mighty One do speak, And to argue for God I delight.
13.4: And yet, you are forgers of falsehood, Physicians of nought--all of you,
13.5: O that you would keep perfectly silent, And it would be to you for wisdom.
13.6: Hear, I pray you, my argument, And to the pleadings of my lips attend,
13.7: For God do you speak perverseness? And for Him do you speak deceit?
13.8: His face do you accept, if for God you strive?
13.9: Is it good that He does search you, If, as one mocks at a man, you mock at Him?
13.10: He does surely reprove you, if in secret you accept faces.
13.11: Does not His excellency terrify you? And His dread fall upon you?
13.12: Your remembrances are similes of ashes, For high places of clay your heights.
13.13: Keep silent from me, and I speak, And pass over me does what?
13.14: Wherefore do I take my flesh in my teeth? And my soul put in my hand?
13.15: Indeed, He does slay me--I wait not! Only, my ways to His face I argue.
13.16: Also--He is to me for salvation, For the profane comes not before Him.
13.17: Hear you diligently my word, And my declaration with your ears.
13.18: Indeed, I pray you, I have set in order the cause, I have known that I am righteous.
13.19: Who is he that does strive with me? For now I keep silent and gasp.
13.20: Only two things, O God, do with me: Then from Your face I am not hidden.
13.21: Your hand put far off from me, And Your terror let not terrify me.
13.22: And call You, and I--I answer, Or--I speak, and answer You me.
13.23: How many iniquities and sins have I? My transgression and my sin let me know.
13.24: Why do You hide Your face? And reckon me for an enemy to You?
13.25: A leaf driven away do You terrify? And the dry stubble do You pursue?
13.26: For You write against me bitter things, And cause me to possess iniquities of my youth:
13.27: And put in the stocks my feet, And observe all my paths, On the roots of my feet You set a print,
13.28: And he, as a rotten thing, wearies away, As a garment has a moth consumed him.

14.1: Man, born of woman! Of few days, and full of trouble!
14.2: As a flower he has gone forth, and is cut off, And he flees as a shadow and stands not.
14.3: Also--on this You have opened Your eyes, And do bring me into judgment with You.
14.4: Who gives a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.
14.5: If determined are his days, The number of his months are with You, His limit You have made, And he passes not over;
14.6: Look away from off him that he may cease, Till he enjoy as an hireling his day.
14.7: For there is of a tree hope, if it be cut down, That again it does change, That its tender branch does not cease.
14.8: If its root becomes old in the earth, And its stem does die in the dust,
14.9: From the fragrance of water it does flourish, And has made a crop as a plant.
14.10: And a man dies, and becomes weak, And man expires, and where is he?
14.11: Waters have gone away from a sea, And a river becomes waste and dry.
14.12: And man has lain down, and rises not, Till the wearing out of the heavens they awake not, Nor are roused from their sleep.
14.13: O that in Sheol You would conceal me, Hide me till the turning of Your anger, Set for me a limit, and remember me.
14.14: If a man dies--does he revive? All days of my warfare I wait, till my change come.
14.15: You do call, and I--I answer You; To the work of Your hands You have desire.
14.16: But now, my steps You number, You do not watch over my sin.
14.17: Sealed up in a bag is my transgression, And You sew up my iniquity.
14.18: And yet, a falling mountain wastes away, And a rock is removed from its place.
14.19: Stones have waters worn away, Their outpourings wash away the dust of earth, And the hope of man You have destroyed.
14.20: You prevail over him for ever, and he goes, He is changing his countenance, And You send him away.
14.21: Honoured are his sons, and he knows not; And they are little, and he attends not to them.
14.22: Only--his flesh for him is pained, And his soul for him does mourn.'

15.1: And Eliphaz the Temanite answers and says: --
15.2: Does a wise man answer with vain knowledge? And fill with an east wind his belly?
15.3: To reason with a word not useful? And speeches--no profit in them?
15.4: Yes, you do make reverence void, And do diminish meditation before God.
15.5: For your mouth teaches your iniquity, And you chooses the tongue of the subtile.
15.6: Your mouth declares you wicked, and not I, And your lips testify against you.
15.7: The first man are you born? And before the heights were you formed?
15.8: Of the secret counsel of God do you hear? And do you withdraw to you wisdom?
15.9: What have you known, and we know not? Do you understand--and it is not with us?
15.10: Both the gray-headed And the very aged are among us--Greater than your father in days.
15.11: Too few for you are the comforts of God? And a gentle word is with you,
15.12: What--does your heart take you away? And what--are yours eyes high?
15.13: For you turn against God your spirit? And have brought out words from your mouth:
15.14: What is man that he is pure, And that he is righteous, one born of woman?
15.15: Indeed, in His holy ones He puts no credence, And the heavens have not been pure in His eyes.
15.16: Also--surely abominable and filthy Is man drinking as water perverseness.
15.17: I show you--hearken to me--And this I have seen and declare:
15.18: Which the wise declare--And have not hid--from their fathers.
15.19: To them alone was the land given, And a stranger passed not over into their midst:
15.20: `All days of the wicked he is paining himself, And few years have been laid up for the terrible one.
15.21: A fearful voice is in his ears, In peace does a destroyer come to him.
15.22: He believes not to return from darkness, And watched is he for the sword.
15.23: He is wandering for bread--`Where is it?' He has known that ready at his hand Is a day of darkness.
15.24: Terrify him do adversity and distress, They prevail over him As a king ready for a boaster.
15.25: For he stretched out against God his hand, And against the Mighty he makes himself mighty.
15.26: He runs to Him with a neck, With thick bosses of his shields.
15.27: For he has covered his face with his fat, And makes vigour over his confidence.
15.28: And he inhabits cities cut off, houses not dwelt in, That have been ready to become heaps.
15.29: He is not rich, nor does his wealth rise, Nor does he stretch out on earth their continuance.
15.30: He turns not aside from darkness, His tender branch does a flame dry up, And he turns aside at the breath of His mouth!
15.31: Let him not put credence in vanity, He has been deceived, For vanity is his recompence.
15.32: Not in his day is it completed, And his bending branch is not green.
15.33: He shakes off as a vine his unripe fruit, And casts off as an olive his blossom.
15.34: For the company of the profane is gloomy, And fire has consumed tents of bribery.
15.35: To conceive misery, and to bear iniquity, Even their heart does prepare deceit.

16.2: I have heard many such things, Miserable comforters are you all.
16.3: Is there an end to words of wind? Or what does embolden you that you answer?
16.4: I also, like you, might speak, If your soul were in my soul's stead. I might join against you with words, And nod at you with my head.
16.5: I might harden you with my mouth, And the moving of my lips might be sparing.
16.6: If I speak, my pain is not restrained, And I cease--what goes from me?
16.7: Only, now, it has wearied me; You have desolated all my company,
16.8: And You do loathe me, For a witness it has been, And rise up against me does my failure, In my face it testifies.
16.9: His anger has torn, and he hates me, He has gnashed at me with his teeth, My adversary sharpens his eyes for me.
16.10: They have gaped on me with their mouth, In reproach they have smitten my cheeks, Together against me they set themselves.
16.11: God shuts me up to the perverse, And to the hands of the wicked turns me over.
16.12: At ease I have been, and he breaks me, And he has laid hold on my neck, And he breaks me in pieces, And he raises me to him for a mark.
16.13: Go round against me do his archers. He splits my reins, and spares not, He pours out to the earth my gall.
16.14: He breaks me--breach upon breach, He runs upon me as a mighty one.
16.15: Sackcloth I have sewed on my skin, And have rolled in the dust my horn.
16.16: My face is foul with weeping, And on my eyelids is death-shade.
16.17: Not for violence in my hands, And my prayer is pure.
16.18: O earth, do not you cover my blood! And let there not be a place for my cry.
16.19: Also, now, indeed, in the heavens is my witness, And my testifier in the high places.
16.20: My interpreter is my friend, To God has my eye dropped:
16.21: And he reasons for a man with God, And a son of man for his friend.
16.22: When a few years do come, Then a path I return not do I go.

17.1: My spirit has been destroyed, My days extinguished--graves are for me.
17.2: If not--mockeries are with me. And in their provocations my eye lodges.
17.3: Place, I pray You, my pledge with You; Who is he that strikes hand with me?
17.4: For their heart You have hidden From understanding, Therefore You do not exalt them.
17.5: For a portion he shows friendship, And the eyes of his sons are consumed.
17.6: And he set me up for a proverb of the peoples, And a wonder before them I am.
17.7: And dim from sorrow is my eye, And my members as a shadow all of them.
17.8: Astonished are the upright at this, And the innocent against the profane Stirs himself up.
17.9: And the righteous lays hold on his way, And the clean of hands adds strength, And--dumb are they all.
17.10: Return, and come in, I pray you, And I find not among you a wise man.
17.11: My days have passed by, My devices have been broken off, The possessions of my heart!
17.12: Night for day they appoint, Light is near because of darkness.
17.13: If I wait--Sheol is my house, In darkness I have spread out my couch.
17.14: To corruption I have called: --`You are my father.' `My mother' and `my sister' --to the worm.
17.15: And where is now my hope? Yes, my hope, who does behold it?
17.16: To the parts of Sheol you go down, If together on the dust we may rest.

18.1: And Bildad the Shuhite answers and says: --
18.2: When do you set an end to words? Consider you, and afterwards do we speak.
18.3: Wherefore have we been reckoned as cattle? We have been defiled in your eyes!
18.4: (He is tearing himself in his anger.) For your sake is earth forsaken? And removed is a rock from its place?
18.5: Also, the light of the wicked is extinguished. And there does not shine a spark of his fire.
18.6: The light has been dark in his tent, And his lamp over him is extinguished.
18.7: Straitened are the steps of his strength, And cast him down does his own counsel.
18.8: For he is sent into a net by his own feet, And on a snare he does walk habitually.
18.9: Seize on the heel does a gin, Prevail over him do the designing.
18.10: Hidden in the earth is his cord, And his trap on the path.
18.11: Round about terrified him have terrors, And they have scattered him--at his feet.
18.12: Hungry is his sorrow, And calamity is ready at his side.
18.13: It consumes the parts of his skin, Consume his parts does death's first-born.
18.14: Drawn from his tent is his confidence, And it causes him to step to the king of terrors.
18.15: It dwells in his tent--out of his provender, Scattered over his habitation is sulphur.
18.16: From beneath his roots are dried up, And from above cut off is his crop.
18.17: His memorial has perished from the land, And he has no name on the street.
18.18: They thrust him from light to darkness, And from the habitable earth cast him out.
18.19: He has no continuator, Nor successor among his people, And none is remaining in his dwellings.
18.20: At this day westerns have been astonished And easterns have taken fright.
18.21: Only these are tabernacles of the perverse, And this the place God has not known.

19.2: Till when do you afflict my soul, And bruise me with words?
19.3: These ten times you put me to shame, you blush not. You make yourselves strange to me--
19.4: And also--truly, I have erred, With me does my error remain.
19.5: If, truly, over me you magnify yourselves, And decide against me my reproach;
19.6: Know now, that God turned me upside down, And His net against me has set round,
19.7: Indeed, I cry out--violence, and am not answered, I cry aloud, and there is no judgment.
19.8: My way He hedged up, and I pass not over, And on my paths darkness He places.
19.9: My honour from off me He has stripped, And He turns the crown from my head.
19.10: He breaks me down round about, and I go, And removes like a tree my hope.
19.11: And He kindles against me His anger, And reckons me to Him as His adversaries.
19.12: Come in do His troops together, And they raise up against me their way, And encamp round about my tent.
19.13: My brethren from me He has put far off, And my acquaintances surely Have been estranged from me.
19.14: Ceased have my neighbours And my familiar friends have forgotten me,
19.15: Sojourners of my house and my maids, For a stranger reckon me: An alien I have been in their eyes.
19.16: To my servant I have called, And he does not answer, With my mouth I make supplication to him.
19.17: My spirit is strange to my wife, And my favours to the sons of my mother's womb.
19.18: Also sucklings have despised me, I rise, and they speak against me.
19.19: Abominate me do all the men of my counsel, And those I have loved, Have been turned against me.
19.20: To my skin and to my flesh Cleaved has my bone, And I deliver myself with the skin of my teeth.
19.21: Pity me, pity me, you my friends, For the hand of God has stricken against me.
19.22: Why do you pursue me as God? And with my flesh are not satisfied?
19.23: Who does grant now, That my words may be written? Who does grant that in a book they may be graven?
19.24: With a pen of iron and lead--For ever in a rock they may be hewn.
19.25: That--I have known my Redeemer, The Living and the Last, For the dust he does rise.
19.26: And after my skin has compassed this body, Then from my flesh I see God:
19.27: Whom I--I see on my side, And my eyes have beheld, and not a stranger, Consumed have been my reins in my bosom.
19.28: But you say, `Why do we pursue after him?' And the root of the matter has been found in me.
19.29: Be you afraid because of the sword, For furious are the punishments of the sword, That you may know that there is a judgment.

20.1: And Zophar the Naamathite answers and says: --
20.2: Therefore my thoughts cause me to answer, And because of my sensations in me.
20.3: The chastisement of my shame I hear, And the spirit of my understanding Does cause me to answer:
20.4: This have you known from antiquity? Since the placing of man on earth?
20.5: That the singing of the wicked is short, And the joy of the profane for a moment,
20.6: Though his excellency go up to the heavens, And his head against a cloud he strike--
20.7: As his own dung for ever he does perish, His beholders say: `Where is he?'
20.8: As a dream he flees, and they find him not, And he is driven away as a vision of the night,
20.9: The eye has not seen him, and adds not. And not again does his place behold him.
20.10: His sons do the poor oppress, And his hands give back his wealth.
20.11: His bones have been full of his youth, And with him on the dust it lies down.
20.12: Though he does sweeten evil in his mouth, Does hide it under his tongue,
20.13: Has pity on it, and does not forsake it, And keep it back in the midst of his palate,
20.14: His food in his bowels is turned, The bitterness of asps is in his heart.
20.15: Wealth he has swallowed, and does vomit it. From his belly God drives it out.
20.16: Gall of asps he sucks, Slay him does the tongue of a viper.
20.17: He looks not on rivulets, Flowing of brooks of honey and butter.
20.18: He is giving back what he laboured for, And does not consume it; As a bulwark is his exchange, and he exults not.
20.19: For he oppressed--he forsook the poor, A house he has taken violently away, And he does not build it.
20.20: For he has not known ease in his belly. With his desirable thing he delivers not himself.
20.21: There is not a remnant to his food, Therefore his good does not stay.
20.22: In the fulness of his sufficiency he is straitened. Every perverse hand does meet him.
20.23: It comes to pass, at the filling of his belly, He sends forth against him The fierceness of His anger, Yes, He rains on him in his eating.
20.24: He flees from an iron weapon, Pass through him does a bow of brass.
20.25: One has drawn, And it comes out from the body, And a glittering weapon from his gall proceeds. On him are terrors.
20.26: All darkness is hid for his treasures, Consume him does a fire not blown, Broken is the remnant in his tent.
20.27: Reveal do the heavens his iniquity, And earth is raising itself against him.
20.28: Remove does the increase of his house, Poured forth in a day of His anger.
20.29: This is the portion of a wicked man from God. And an inheritance appointed him by God.

21.2: Hear you diligently my word, And this is your consolation.
21.3: Bear with me, and I speak, And after my speaking--you may deride.
21.4: I--to man is my complaint? and if so, wherefore May not my temper become short?
21.5: Turn to me, and be astonished, And put hand to mouth.
21.6: Yes, if I have remembered, then I have been troubled. And my flesh has taken fright.
21.7: Wherefore do the wicked live? They have become old, Yes, they have been mighty in wealth.
21.8: Their seed is established, Before their face with them, And their offspring before their eyes.
21.9: Their houses are peace without fear, Nor is a rod of God upon them.
21.10: His bullock has eaten corn, and does not loath. His cow brings forth safely, And does not miscarry.
21.11: They send forth as a flock their sucklings, And their children skip,
21.12: They lift themselves up at timbrel and harp, And rejoice at the sound of an organ.
21.13: They wear out in good their days, And in a moment to Sheol go down.
21.14: And they say to God, `Turn aside from us, And the knowledge of Your ways We have not desired.
21.15: What is the Mighty One that we serve Him? And what do we profit when we meet with Him?'
21.16: Indeed, not in their hand is their good, (The counsel of the wicked Has been far from me.)
21.17: How oft is the lamp of the wicked extinguished, And come on them does their calamity? Pangs He apportions in His anger.
21.18: They are as straw before wind, And as chaff a hurricane has stolen away,
21.19: God lays up for his sons his sorrow, He gives recompense to him--and he knows.
21.20: His own eyes see his destruction, And of the wrath of the Mighty he drinks.
21.21: For what is his delight in his house after him, And the number of his months cut off?
21.22: To God does one teach knowledge, And He the high does judge?
21.23: This one dies in his perfect strength, Wholly at ease and quiet.
21.24: His breasts have been full of milk, And marrow his bones does moisten.
21.25: And this one dies with a bitter soul, And have not eaten with gladness.
21.26: Together--on the dust they lie down, And the worm does cover them over.
21.27: Indeed, I have known your thoughts, And the devices against me you do wrongfully.
21.28: For you say, `Where is the house of the noble? And where the tent--The tabernacles of the wicked?'
21.29: Have you not asked those passing by the way? And their signs do you not know?
21.30: That to a day of calamity is the wicked spared. To a day of wrath they are brought.
21.31: Who does declare to his face his way? And for that which he has done, Who does give recompence to him?
21.32: And he--to the graves he is brought. And over the heap a watch is kept.
21.33: Sweet to him have been the clods of the valley, And after him every man he draws, And before him there is no numbering.
21.34: And how do you comfort me with vanity, And in your answers has been left trespass?

22.1: And Eliphaz the Temanite answers and says: --
22.2: To God is a man profitable, Because a wise man to himself is profitable?
22.3: Is it a delight to the Mighty One That you are righteous? is it gain, That you make perfect your ways?
22.4: Because of your reverence Does He reason with you? He enters with you into judgment:
22.5: Is not your wickedness abundant? And there is no end to your iniquities.
22.6: For you take a pledge of your brother for nought, And the garments of the naked You do strip off.
22.7: You cause not the weary to drink water, And from the hungry you withhold bread.
22.8: As to the man of arm--he has the earth, And the accepted of face--he dwells in it.
22.9: Widows you have sent away empty, And the arms of the fatherless are bruised.
22.10: Therefore round about you are snares, And trouble you does fear suddenly.
22.11: Or darkness--you do not see, And abundance of waters does cover you.
22.12: Is not God high in heaven? And see the summit of the stars, That they are high.
22.13: And you have said, `What--has God known? Through thickness does He judge?
22.14: Thick clouds are a secret place to Him, And He does not see;' And the circle of the heavens He walks habitually,
22.15: The path of the age do you observe, That men of iniquity have trodden?
22.16: Who have been cut down unexpectedly, A flood is poured out on their foundation.
22.17: Those saying to God, `Turn aside from us,' And what does the Mighty One to them?
22.18: And he has filled their houses with good: (And the counsel of the wicked Has been far from me.)
22.19: See do the righteous and they rejoice, And the innocent mocks at them,
22.20: `Surely our substance has not been cut off, And their excellency has fire consumed.'
22.21: Acquaint yourself, I pray you, with Him, And be at peace, Thereby your increase is good.
22.22: Receive, I pray you, from His mouth a law, And set His sayings in your heart.
22.23: If you do return to the Mighty You are built up, You put iniquity far from your tents.
22.24: So as to set on the dust a defence, And on a rock of the valleys a covering.
22.25: And the Mighty has been your defence, And silver is strength to you.
22.26: For then on the Mighty you delight yourself, And do lift up to God your face,
22.27: You do make supplication to Him, And He does hear you, And your vows you complete.
22.28: And you decree a saying, And it is established to you, And on your ways has light shone.
22.29: For they have made low, And you say, `Lift up.' And the bowed down of eyes he saves.
22.30: He delivers the not innocent, Yes, he has been delivered By the cleanness of your hands.

23.2: Also--to-day is my complaint bitter, My hand has been heavy because of my sighing.
23.3: O that I had known--and I find Him, I come in to His seat,
23.4: I arrange before Him the cause, And my mouth fill with arguments.
23.5: I know the words He does answer me, And understand what He says to me.
23.6: In the abundance of power does He strive with me? No! surely He puts it in me.
23.7: There the upright does reason with Him, And I escape for ever from my judge.
23.8: Indeed, forward I go--and He is not, And backward--and I perceive him not.
23.9: To the left in His working--and I see not, He is covered on the right, and I behold not.
23.10: For He has known the way with me, He has tried me--as gold I go forth.
23.11: On His step has my foot laid hold, His way I have kept, and turn not aside,
23.12: The command of His lips, and I depart not. Above my allotted portion I have laid up The sayings of His mouth.
23.13: And He is in one mind, And who does turn Him back? And His soul has desired--and He does it.
23.14: For He does complete my portion, And many such things are with Him.
23.15: Therefore, from His presence I am troubled, I consider, and am afraid of Him.
23.16: And God has made my heart soft, And the Mighty has troubled me.
23.17: For I have not been cut off before darkness, And before me He covered thick darkness.

24.1: Wherefore from the Mighty One Times have not been hidden, And those knowing Him have not seen His days.
24.2: The borders they reach, A drove they have taken violently away, Yes, they do evil.
24.3: The ass of the fatherless they lead away, They take in pledge the ox of the widow,
24.4: They turn aside the needy from the way, Together have hid the poor of the earth.
24.5: Indeed, wild asses in a wilderness, They have gone out about their work, Seeking early for prey, A mixture for himself--food for young ones.
24.6: In a field his provender they reap, And the vineyard of the wicked they glean.
24.7: The naked they cause to lodge Without clothing. And there is no covering in the cold.
24.8: From the inundation of hills they are wet, And without a refuge--have embraced a rock.
24.9: They take violently away From the breast the orphan, And on the poor they lay a pledge.
24.10: Naked, they have gone without clothing, And hungry--have taken away a sheaf.
24.11: Between their walls they make oil, Wine-presses they have trodden, and thirst.
24.12: Because of enmity men do groan, And the soul of pierced ones does cry, And God does not give praise.
24.13: They have been among rebellious ones of light, They have not discerned His ways, Nor abode in His paths.
24.14: At the light does the murderer rise, He does slay the poor and needy, And in the night he is as a thief.
24.15: And the eye of an adulterer Has observed the twilight, Saying, `No eye does behold me.' And he puts the face in secret.
24.16: He has dug in the darkness--houses; By day they shut themselves up, They have not known light.
24.17: When together, morning is to them death shade, When he discerns the terrors of death shade.
24.18: Light he is on the face of the waters, Vilified is their portion in the earth, He turns not the way of vineyards.
24.19: Drought--also heat--consume snow-waters, Sheol those who have sinned.
24.20: Forget him does the womb, Sweeten on him does the worm, No more is he remembered, And broken as a tree is wickedness.
24.21: Treating evil the barren who bears not, And to the widow he does no good,
24.22: And has drawn the mighty by his power, He rises, and none believes in life.
24.23: He gives to him confidence, and he is supported, And his eyes are on their ways.
24.24: High they were for a little, and they are not, And they have been brought low. As all others they are shut up, And as the head of an ear of corn cut off.
24.25: And if not now, who does prove me a liar, And does make of nothing my word?

25.1: And Bildad the Shuhite answers and says: --
25.2: The rule and fear are with Him, Making peace in His high places.
25.3: Is their any number to His troops? And on whom arises not His light?
25.4: And what? is man righteous with God? And what? is he pure--born of a woman?
25.5: Indeed--to the moon, and it shines not, And stars have not been pure in His eyes.
25.6: How much less man--a grub, And the son of man--a worm!

26.2: What--you have helped the powerless, Saved an arm not strong!
26.3: What--you have given counsel to the unwise, And wise plans in abundance made known.
26.4: With whom have you declared words? And whose breath came forth from you?
26.5: The Rephaim are formed, Beneath the waters, also their inhabitants.
26.6: Naked is Sheol over-against Him, And there is no covering to destruction.
26.7: Stretching out the north over desolation, Hanging the earth upon nothing,
26.8: Binding up the waters in His thick clouds, And the cloud is not rent under them.
26.9: Taking hold of the face of the throne, Spreading over it His cloud.
26.10: A limit He has placed on the waters, To the boundary of light with darkness.
26.11: Pillars of the heavens do tremble, And they wonder because of His rebuke.
26.12: By His power He has quieted the sea, And by His understanding smitten the proud.
26.13: By His Spirit the heavens He beautified, Formed has His hand the fleeing serpent.
26.14: Indeed, these are the borders of His way, And how little a matter is heard of Him, And the thunder of His might Who does understand?

27.1: And Job adds to lift up his simile, and says: --
27.2: God lives! He turned aside my judgment, And the Mighty--He made my soul bitter.
27.3: For all the while my breath is in me, And the spirit of God in my nostrils.
27.4: My lips do not speak perverseness, And my tongue does not utter deceit.
27.5: Pollution to me--if I justify you, Till I expire I turn not aside my integrity from me.
27.6: On my righteousness I have laid hold, And I do not let it go, My heart does not reproach me while I live.
27.7: As the wicked is my enemy, And my withstander as the perverse.
27.8: For what is the hope of the profane, When He does cut off? When God does cast off his soul?
27.9: His cry does God hear, When distress comes on him?
27.10: On the Mighty does he delight himself? Call God at all times?
27.11: I show you by the hand of God, That which is with the Mighty I hide not.
27.12: Indeed, you--all of you--have seen, And why is this--you are altogether vain?
27.13: This is the portion of wicked man with God, And the inheritance of terrible ones From the Mighty they receive.
27.14: If his sons multiply--for them is a sword. And his offspring are not satisfied with bread.
27.15: His remnant in death are buried, And his widows do not weep.
27.16: If he heap up as dust silver, And as clay prepare clothing,
27.17: He prepares--and the righteous puts it on, And the silver the innocent does apportion.
27.18: He has built as a moth his house, And as a booth a watchman has made.
27.19: Rich he lies down, and he is not gathered, His eyes he has opened, and he is not.
27.20: Overtake him as waters do terrors, By night stolen him away has a whirlwind.
27.21: Take him up does an east wind, and he goes, And it frightens him from his place,
27.22: And it casts at him, and does not spare, From its hand he diligently flees.
27.23: It claps at him its hands, And it hises at him from his place.

28.1: Surely there is for silver a source, And a place for the gold they refine;
28.2: Iron from the dust is taken, And from the firm stone brass.
28.3: An end has he set to darkness, And to all perfection he is searching, A stone of darkness and death-shade.
28.4: A stream has broken out from a sojourner, Those forgotten of the foot, They were low, from man they wandered.
28.5: The earth! from it comes forth bread, And its under-part is turned like fire.
28.6: A place of the sapphire are its stones, And it has dust of gold.
28.7: A path--not known it has a ravenous fowl, Nor scorched it has an eye of the kite,
28.8: Nor trodden it have the sons of pride, Not passed over it has the fierce lion.
28.9: Against the flint he sent forth his hand, He overturned from the root mountains.
28.10: Among rocks, brooks he has cleaved, And every precious thing has his eye seen.
28.11: From overflowing floods he has bound, And the hidden thing brings out to light.
28.12: And the wisdom--from where is it found? And where is this, the place of understanding?
28.13: Man has not known its arrangement, Nor is it found in the land of the living.
28.14: The deep has said, `It is not in me,' And the sea has said, `It is not with me.'
28.15: Gold is not given for it, Nor is silver weighed--its price.
28.16: It is not valued with pure gold of Ophir, With precious onyx and sapphire,
28.17: Not equal it do gold and crystal, Nor is its exchange a vessel of fine gold.
28.18: Corals and pearl are not remembered, The acquisition of wisdom is above rubies.
28.19: Not equal it does the topaz of Cush, With pure gold it is not valued.
28.20: And the wisdom--from where does it come? And where is this, the place of understanding?
28.21: It has been hid from the eyes of all living. And from the fowl of the heavens It has been hidden.
28.22: Destruction and death have said: `With our ears we have heard its fame.'
28.23: God has understood its way, And He has known its place.
28.24: For He to the ends of the earth does look, Under the whole heavens He does see,
28.25: To make for the wind a weight, And the waters He meted out in measure.
28.26: In His making for the rain a limit, And a way for the brightness of the voices,
28.27: Then He has seen and declares it, He has prepared it, and also searched it out,
28.28: And He says to man: --`Indeed, fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, And to turn from evil is understanding.'

29.1: And Job adds to lift up his simile, and says: --
29.2: Who does make me as in months past, As in the days of God's preserving me?
29.3: In His causing His lamp to shine on my head, By His light I walk through darkness.
29.4: As I have been in days of my maturity, And the counsel of God upon my tent.
29.5: When yet the Mighty One is with me. Round about me--my young ones,
29.6: When washing my goings with butter, And the firm rock is with me rivulets of oil.
29.7: When I go out to the gate by the city, In a broad place I prepare my seat.
29.8: Seen me have youths, and they, been hidden, And the aged have risen--they stood up.
29.9: Princes have kept in words, And a hand they place on their mouth.
29.10: The voice of leaders has been hidden, And their tongue to the palate has cleaved.
29.11: For the ear heard, and declares me happy, And the eye has seen, and testifies to me.
29.12: For I deliver the afflicted who is crying, And the fatherless who has no helper.
29.13: The blessing of the perishing comes on me, And the heart of the widow I cause to sing.
29.14: Righteousness I have put on, and it clothes me, As a robe and a diadem my justice.
29.15: Eyes I have been to the blind, And feet to the lame am I.
29.16: A father I am to the needy, And the cause I have not known I search out.
29.17: And I break the jaw-teeth of the perverse, And from his teeth I cast away prey.
29.18: And I say, `With my nest I expire, And as the sand I multiply days.'
29.19: My root is open to the waters, And dew does lodge on my branch.
29.20: My honour is fresh with me, And my bow in my hand is renewed.
29.21: To me they have hearkened, Yes, they wait, and are silent for my counsel.
29.22: After my word they change not, And on them does my speech drop,
29.23: And they wait as for rain for me, And their mouth they have opened wide As for the latter rain.
29.24: I laugh to them--they give no credence, And the light of my face cause not to fall.
29.25: I choose their way, and sit head, And I dwell as a king in a troop, When mourners he does comfort.

30.1: And now, laughed at me, Have the younger in days than I, Whose fathers I have loathed to set With the dogs of my flock.
30.2: Also--the power of their hands, why is it to me? On them has old age perished.
30.3: With want and with famine gloomy, Those fleeing to a dry place, Formerly a desolation and waste,
30.4: Those cropping mallows near a shrub, And broom-roots is their food.
30.5: From the midst they are cast out, (They shout against them as a thief),
30.6: In a frightful place of valleys to dwell, Holes of earth and clefts.
30.7: Among shrubs they do groan, Under nettles they are gathered together.
30.8: Sons of folly--even sons without name, They have been smitten from the land.
30.9: And now, their song I have been, And I am to them for a byword.
30.10: They have abominated me, They have kept far from me, And from before me have not spared to spit.
30.11: Because His cord He loosed and afflicts me, And the bridle from before me, They have cast away.
30.12: On the right hand does a brood arise, My feet they have cast away, And they raise up against me, Their paths of calamity.
30.13: They have broken down my path, By my calamity they profit, `He has no helper.'
30.14: As a wide breach they come, Under the desolation have rolled themselves.
30.15: He has turned against me terrors, It pursues as the wind my abundance, And as a thick cloud, Has my safety passed away.
30.16: And now, in me my soul pours itself out, Seize me do days of affliction.
30.17: At night my bone has been pierced in me, And my eyelids do not lie down.
30.18: By the abundance of power, Is my clothing changed, As the mouth of my coat it does gird me.
30.19: Casting me into mire, And I am become like dust and ashes.
30.20: I cry to You, And You do not answer me, I have stood, and You do consider me.
30.21: You are turned to be fierce to me, With the strength of Your hand, You oppress me.
30.22: You do lift me up, On the wind You do cause me to ride, And You melt--You level me.
30.23: For I have known To death You do bring me back, And to the house appointed for all living.
30.24: Surely not against the heap Does He send forth the hand, Though in its ruin they have safety.
30.25: Did not I weep for him whose day is hard? Grieved has my soul for the needy.
30.26: When good I expected, then comes evil, And I wait for light, and darkness comes.
30.27: My bowels have boiled, and have not ceased, Gone before me have days of affliction.
30.28: Mourning I have gone without the sun, I have risen, in an assembly I cry.
30.29: A brother I have been to dragons, And a companion to daughters of the ostrich.
30.30: My skin has been black upon me, And my bone has burned from heat,
30.31: And my harp does become mourning, And my organ the sound of weeping.

31.1: A covenant I made for my eyes, And what--do I attend to a virgin?
31.2: And what is the portion of God from above? And the inheritance of the Mighty from the heights?
31.3: Is not calamity to the perverse? And strangeness to workers of iniquity?
31.4: Does not He see my ways, And all my steps number?
31.5: If I have walked with vanity, And my foot does hasten to deceit,
31.6: He does weigh me in righteous balances, And God does know my integrity.
31.7: If my step does turn aside from the way, And after my eyes has my heart gone, And to my hands cleaved has blemish,
31.8: Let me sow--and another eat, And my products let be rooted out.
31.9: If my heart has been enticed by woman, And by the opening of my neighbour I laid wait,
31.10: Grind to another let my wife, And over her let others bend.
31.11: For it is a wicked thing, and a judicial iniquity;
31.12: For a fire it is, to destruction it consumes, And among all my increase does take root,
31.13: If I despise the cause of my man-servant, And of my handmaid, In their contending with me,
31.14: Then what do I do when God arises? And when He does inspect, What do I answer Him?
31.15: Did not He that made me in the womb make him? Yes, prepare us in the womb does One.
31.16: If I withhold from pleasure the poor, And the eyes of the widow do consume,
31.17: And I do eat my morsel by myself, And the orphan has not eat of it,
31.18: (But from my youth He grew up with me as with a father, And from the belly of my mother I am led.)
31.19: If I see any perishing without clothing, And there is no covering to the needy,
31.20: If his loins have not blessed me, And from the fleece of my sheep He does not warm himself,
31.21: If I have waved at the fatherless my hand, When I see in him the gate of my court,
31.22: My shoulder from its blade let fall, And my arm from the bone be broken.
31.23: For a dread to me is calamity from God, And because of His excellency I am not able.
31.24: If I have made gold my confidence, And to the pure gold have said, `My trust,'
31.25: If I rejoice because great is my wealth, And because abundance has my hand found,
31.26: If I see the light when it shines, And the precious moon walking,
31.27: And my heart is enticed in secret, And my hand does kiss my mouth,
31.28: It also is a judicial iniquity, For I had lied to God above.
31.29: If I rejoice at the ruin of my hater, And stirred up myself when evil found him,
31.30: Yes, I have not suffered my mouth to sin, To ask with an oath his life.
31.31: If not--say you, O men of my tent, `O that we had of his flesh, we are not satisfied.'
31.32: In the street does not lodge a stranger, My doors to the traveller I open.
31.33: If I have covered as Adam my transgressions, To hide in my bosom my iniquity,
31.34: Because I fear a great multitude, And the contempt of families does affright me, Then I am silent, I go not out of the opening.
31.35: Who gives to me a hearing? indeed, my mark. The Mighty One does answer me, And a bill has my adversary written.
31.36: If not--on my shoulder I take it up, I bind it a crown on myself.
31.37: The number of my steps I tell Him, As a leader I approach Him.
31.38: If against me my land does cry out, And together its furrows weep,
31.39: If its strength I consumed without money, And the life of its possessors, I have caused to breathe out,
31.40: Instead of wheat let a thorn go forth, And instead of barley a useless weed! The words of Job are finished.

32.1: And these three men cease from answering Job, for he is righteous in his own eyes,
32.2: and burn does the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram; against Job has his anger burned, because of his justifying himself more than God;
32.3: and against his three friends has his anger burned, because that they have not found an answer, and condemn Job.
32.4: And Elihu has waited earnestly beside Job with words, for they are older than he in days.
32.5: And Elihu sees that there is no answer in the mouth of the three men, and his anger burns.
32.6: And Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answers and says: --Young I am in days, and you are age Therefore I have feared, And am afraid of shewing you my opinion.
32.7: I said: Days do speak, And multitude of years teach wisdom.
32.8: Surely a spirit is in man, And the breath of the Mighty One Does cause them to understand.
32.9: The multitude are not wise, Nor do the aged understand judgment.
32.10: Therefore I have said: Hearken to me, I do show my opinion--even I.
32.11: Indeed, I have waited for your words, I give ear to your reasons, Till you search out sayings.
32.12: And to you I attend, And indeed, there is no reasoner for Job, Or answerer of his sayings among you.
32.13: Lest you say, We have found wisdom, God does thrust him away, not man.
32.14: And he has not set in array words for me, And with your sayings I do not answer him.
32.15: (They have broken down, They have not answered again, They removed from themselves words.
32.16: And I have waited, but they do not speak, For they have stood still, They have not answered any more.)
32.17: I answer, even I--my share, I show my opinion--even I.
32.18: For I have been full of words, Distressed me has the spirit of my breast,
32.19: Indeed, my breast is as wine not opened, Like new bottles it is broken up.
32.20: I speak, and there is refreshment to me, I open my lips and answer.
32.21: Let me not, I pray you, accept the face of any, Nor to man give flattering titles,
32.22: For I have not known to give flattering titles, In a little does my Maker take me away.

33.1: And yet, I pray you, O Job, Hear my speech and to all my words give ear.
33.2: Indeed, I pray you, I have opened my mouth, My tongue has spoken in the palate.
33.3: Of the uprightness of my heart are my sayings, And knowledge have my lips clearly spoken.
33.4: The Spirit of God has made me, And the breath of the Mighty does quicken me.
33.5: If you are able--answer me, Set in array before me--station yourself.
33.6: Indeed, I am, according to your word, for God, From the clay I--I also, have been formed.
33.7: Indeed, my terror does not frighten you, And my burden on you is not heavy.
33.8: Surely--you have said in my ears, And the sounds of words I hear:
33.9: `Pure am I, without transgression, Innocent am I, and I have no iniquity.
33.10: Indeed, occasions against me He does find, He does reckon me for an enemy to Him,
33.11: He does put in the stocks my feet, He does watch all my paths.'
33.12: Indeed, in this you have not been righteous, I answer you, that greater is God than man.
33.13: Wherefore against Him have you striven, When for all His matters He answers not?
33.14: For once does God speak, and twice, (He does not behold it.)
33.15: In a dream--a vision of night, In the falling of deep sleep on men, In slumberings on a bed.
33.16: Then He uncovers the ear of men, And for their instruction seals:
33.17: To turn aside man from doing, And pride from man He conceals.
33.18: He keeps back his soul from corruption, And his life from passing away by a dart.
33.19: And he has been reproved With pain on his bed, And the strife of his bones is enduring.
33.20: And his life has nauseated bread, And his soul desirable food.
33.21: His flesh is consumed from being seen, And high are his bones, they were not seen!
33.22: And draw near to the pit does his soul, And his life to those causing death.
33.23: If there is by him a messenger, An interpreter--one of a thousand, To declare for man his uprightness:
33.24: Then He does favour him and says, `Ransom him from going down to the pit, I have found an atonement.'
33.25: Fresher is his flesh than a child's, He returns to the days of his youth.
33.26: He makes supplication to God, And He accepts him. And he sees His face with shouting, And He returns to man His righteousness.
33.27: He looks on men, and says, `I sinned, And uprightness I have perverted, And it has not been profitable to me.
33.28: He has ransomed my soul From going over into the pit, And my life on the light looks.'
33.29: Indeed, all these does God work, Twice--thrice with man,
33.30: To bring back his soul from the pit, To be enlightened with the light of the living.
33.31: Attend, O Job, hearken to me, Keep silent, and I--I do speak.
33.32: If there are words--answer me, Speak, for I have a desire to justify you.
33.33: If there are not--hearken you to me, Keep silent, and I teach you wisdom.

34.2: Hear, O wise men, my words, And, O knowing ones, give ear to me.
34.3: For the ear does try words, And the palate tastes to eat.
34.4: Judgment let us choose for ourselves, Let us know among ourselves what is good.
34.5: For Job has said, `I have been righteous, And God has turned aside my right,
34.6: Against my right do I lie? Mortal is my arrow--without transgression.'
34.7: Who is a man like Job? He drinks scoffing like water,
34.8: And he has travelled for company With workers of iniquity, So as to go with men of wickedness.
34.9: For he has said, `It does not profit a man, When he delights himself with God.'
34.10: Therefore, O men of heart, hearken to me; Far be it from God to do wickedness, And from the Mighty to do perverseness:
34.11: For the work of man he repays to him, And according to the path of each He does cause him to find.
34.12: Yes, truly, God does not do wickedly, And the Mighty does not pervert judgment.
34.13: Who has inspected for Himself the earth? And who has placed all the habitable world?
34.14: If He does set on him His heart, His spirit and his breath to Him He gathers.
34.15: Expire does all flesh together, And man to dust returns.
34.16: And if there is understanding, hear this, Give ear to the voice of my words.
34.17: Yes, does one hating justice govern? Or the Most Just do you condemn?
34.18: Who has said to a king--`Worthless,' To princes--`Wicked?'
34.19: That has not accepted the person of princes, Nor has known the rich before the poor, For a work of His hands are all of them.
34.20: In a moment they die, and at midnight Shake do people, and they pass away, And they remove the mighty without hand.
34.21: For His eyes are on the ways of each, And all his steps He does see.
34.22: There is no darkness nor death-shade, For workers of iniquity to be hidden there;
34.23: For He does not suffer man any more, To go to God in judgment,
34.24: He breaks the mighty--no searching! And He appoints others in their stead.
34.25: Therefore He knows their works, And He has overturned by night, And they are bruised.
34.26: As wicked He has stricken them, In the place of beholders.
34.27: Because that against right They have turned aside from after Him, And none of His ways have considered wisely,
34.28: To cause to come in to Him The cry of the poor, And the cry of the afflicted He hears.
34.29: And He gives rest, and who makes wrong? And hides the face, and who beholds it? And in reference to a nation and to a man, It is the same.
34.30: From the reigning of a profane man, From the snares of a people;
34.31: For to God has any said: `I have taken away, I do not corruptly,
34.32: Besides that which I see, show You me, If iniquity I have done--I do not add?'
34.33: By you does He recompense, That you have refused--That you do choose, and not I? And what you have known, speak.
34.34: Let men of heart say to me, And a wise man is hearkening to me.
34.35: Job--not with knowledge does he speak, And his words are not with wisdom.
34.36: My Father! let Job be tried--to victory, Because of answers for men of iniquity,
34.37: For he does add to his sin, Transgression among us he vomits, And multiplies his sayings to God.

35.2: This have you reckoned for judgment: You have said--`My righteousness is more than God's?'
35.3: For you say, `What does it profit You! What do I profit from my sin?'
35.4: I return you words, and your friends with you,
35.5: Behold attentively the heavens--and see, And behold the clouds, They have been higher than you.
35.6: If you have sinned, what do you against Him? And your transgressions have been multiplied, What do you to Him?
35.7: If you have been righteous, What do you give to Him? Or what from your hand does He receive?
35.8: For a man like yourself is your wickedness, And for a son of man your righteousness.
35.9: Because of the multitude of oppressions They cause to cry out, They cry because of the arm of the mighty.
35.10: And none said, `Where is God my maker? Giving songs in the night,
35.11: Teaching us more than the beasts of the earth, Yes, than the fowl of the heavens He makes us wiser.'
35.12: There they cry, and He does not answer, Because of the pride of evil doers.
35.13: Surely vanity God does not hear, And the Mighty does not behold it.
35.14: Yes, though you do you say do not behold Him, Judgment is before Him, and stay for Him.
35.15: And, now, because there is not, He has appointed His anger, And He has not known in great extremity.
35.16: And Job with vanity does open his mouth, Without knowledge words he multiplies.

36.2: Honour me a little, and I show you, That yet for God are words.
36.3: I lift up my knowledge from afar, And to my Maker I ascribe righteousness.
36.4: For, truly, my words are not false, The perfect in knowledge is with you.
36.5: Indeed, God is mighty, and despises not, Mighty in power and heart.
36.6: He revives not the wicked, And the judgment of the poor appoints;
36.7: He withdraws not from the righteous His eyes, And from kings on the throne, And causes them to sit for ever, and they are high,
36.8: And if prisoners in fetters They are captured with cords of affliction,
36.9: Then He declares to them their work, And their transgressions, Because they have become mighty,
36.10: And He uncovers their ear for instruction, And says that they turn back from iniquity.
36.11: If they do hear and serve, They complete their days in good, And their years in pleasantness.
36.12: And if they do not hearken, By the dart they pass away, And expire without knowledge.
36.13: And the profane in heart set the face, They cry not when He has bound them.
36.14: Their soul dies in youth, And their life among the defiled.
36.15: He draws out the afflicted in his affliction, And uncovers in oppression their ear.
36.16: And also He moved you from a strait place, To a broad place--no straitness under it, And the sitting beyond of your table Has been full of fatness.
36.17: And the judgment of the wicked you have fulfilled, Judgment and justice are upheld--because of fury,
36.18: Lest He move you with a stroke, And the abundance of an atonement turn you not aside.
36.19: Does He value your riches? He has gold, and all the forces of power.
36.20: Desire not the night, For the going up of peoples in their stead.
36.21: Take heed--do not turn to iniquity, For on this you have fixed Rather than on affliction.
36.22: Indeed, God does sit on high by His power, Who is like Him--a teacher?
36.23: Who has appointed to Him his way? And who said, `You have done iniquity?'
36.24: Remember that you magnify His work That men have beheld.
36.25: All men have looked on it, Man looks attentively from afar.
36.26: Indeed, God is high, And we know not the number of His years, Yes, there is no searching.
36.27: When He does diminish droppings of the waters, They refine rain according to its vapour,
36.28: Which clouds do drop, They distil on man abundantly.
