36.29: Yes, does any understand The spreadings out of a cloud? The noises of His tabernacle?
36.30: Indeed, He has spread over it His light, And the roots of the sea He has covered,
36.31: For by them He does judge peoples, He gives food in abundance.
36.32: By two palms He has covered the light, And lays a charge over it in meeting,
36.33: He shows by it to his friend substance, Anger against perversity.

37.1: Also, at this my heart trembles, And it moves from its place.
37.2: Hearken diligently to the trembling of His voice, Yes, the sound from His mouth goes forth.
37.3: Under the whole heavens He directs it, And its light is over the skirts of the earth.
37.4: After it roar does a voice--He thunders with the voice of His excellency, And He does not hold them back, When His voice is heard.
37.5: God thunders with His voice wonderfully, Doing great things and we know not.
37.6: For to snow He says, `Be on the earth.' And the small rain and great rain of His power.
37.7: Into the hand of every man he seals, For the knowledge by all men of His work.
37.8: And enter does the beast into covert, And in its habitations it does continue.
37.9: From the inner chamber comes a hurricane, And from scatterings winds--cold,
37.10: From the breath of God is frost given, And the breadth of waters is straitened,
37.11: Yes, by filling He does press out a cloud, Scatter a cloud does His light.
37.12: And it is turning itself round by His counsels, For their doing all He commands them, On the face of the habitable earth.
37.13: Whether for a rod, or for His land, Or for kindness--He does cause it to come.
37.14: Hear this, O Job, Stand and consider the wonders of God.
37.15: Do you know when God does place them, And caused to shine the light of His cloud?
37.16: Do you know the balancings of a cloud? The wonders of the Perfect in knowledge?
37.17: How your garments are warm, In the quieting of the earth from the south?
37.18: You have made an expanse with Him For the clouds--strong as a hard mirror!
37.19: Let us know what we say to Him, We set not in array because of darkness.
37.20: Is it declared to Him that I speak? If a man has spoken, surely he is swallowed up.
37.21: And now, they have not seen the light, Bright it is in the clouds, And the wind has passed by and cleanses them.
37.22: From the golden north it comes, Beside God is fearful honour.
37.23: The Mighty! we have not found Him out, High in power and judgment, He does not answer! And abundant in righteousness,
37.24: Therefore do men fear Him, He sees not any of the wise of heart.

38.1: And Jehovah answers Job out of the whirlwind, and says: --
38.2: Who is this--darkening counsel, By words without knowledge?
38.3: Gird, I pray you, as a man, your loins, And I ask you, and cause you Me to know.
38.4: Where were you when I founded earth? Declare, if you have known understanding.
38.5: Who placed its measures--if you know? Or who has stretched out upon it a line?
38.6: On what have its sockets been sunk? Or who has cast its corner-stone?
38.7: In the singing together of stars of morning, And all sons of God shout for joy,
38.8: And He shuts up with doors the sea, In its coming forth, from the womb it goes out.
38.9: In My making a cloud its clothing, And thick darkness its swaddling band,
38.10: And I measure over it My statute, And place bar and doors,
38.11: And say, `Hitherto come you, and add not, And a command is placed On the pride of your billows.'
38.12: Have you commanded morning since your days? Do you cause the dawn to know its place?
38.13: To take hold on the skirts of the earth, And the wicked are shaken out of it,
38.14: It turns itself as clay of a seal And they station themselves as clothed.
38.15: And withheld from the wicked is their light, And the arm lifted up is broken.
38.16: Have you come in to springs of the sea? And in searching the deep Have you walked up and down?
38.17: Revealed to you were the gates of death? And the gates of death-shade do you see?
38.18: You have understanding, Even to the broad places of earth! Declare--if you have known it all.
38.19: Where is this--the way light dwells? And darkness, where is this--its place?
38.20: That you do take it to its boundary, And that you do understand The paths of its house.
38.21: You have known--for then you are born And the number of your days are many!
38.22: Have you come in to the treasure of snow? Yes, the treasures of hail do you see?
38.23: That I have kept back for a time of distress, For a day of conflict and battle.
38.24: Where is this, the way light is apportioned? It scatters an east wind over the earth.
38.25: Who has divided for the flood a conduit? And a way for the lightning of the voices?
38.26: To cause it to rain on a land--no man, A wilderness--no man in it.
38.27: To satisfy a desolate and waste place, And to cause to shoot up The produce of the tender grass?
38.28: Has the rain a father? Or who has begotten the drops of dew?
38.29: From whose belly came forth the ice? And the hoar-frost of the heavens, Who has begotten it?
38.30: As a stone waters are hidden, And the face of the deep is captured.
38.31: Do you bind sweet influences of Kimah? Or the attractions of Kesil do you open?
38.32: Do you bring out Mazzaroth in its season? And Aysh for her sons do you comfort?
38.33: Have you known the statutes of heaven? Or do you appoint Its dominion in the earth?
38.34: Do you lift up to the cloud your voice, And abundance of water does cover you?
38.35: Do you send out lightnings, and they go And say to you, `Behold us?'
38.36: Who has put in the inward parts wisdom? Or who has given To the covered part understanding?
38.37: Who does number the clouds by wisdom? And the bottles of the heavens, Who does cause to lie down,
38.38: In the hardening of dust into hardness, And clods cleave together?
38.39: Do you hunt for a lion prey? And the desire of young lions fulfil?
38.40: When they bow down in dens--Abide in a thicket for a covert?
38.41: Who does prepare for a raven his provision, When his young ones cry to God? They wander without food.

39.1: Have you known the time of The bearing of the wild goats of the rock? The bringing forth of hinds you do mark!
39.2: You do number the months they fulfil? And you have known the time of their bringing forth!
39.3: They bow down, Their young ones they bring forth safely, Their pangs they cast forth.
39.4: Safe are their young ones, They grow up in the field, they have gone out, And have not returned to them.
39.5: Who has sent forth the wild ass free? Yes, the bands of the wild ass who opened?
39.6: Whose house I have made the wilderness, And his dwellings the barren land,
39.7: He does laugh at the multitude of a city, The cries of an exactor he hears not.
39.8: The range of mountains is his pasture, And after every green thing he seeks.
39.9: Is a Reem willing to serve you? Does he lodge by your crib?
39.10: Do you bind a Reem in a furrow with his thick band? Does he harrow valleys after you?
39.11: Do you trust in him because great is his power? And do you leave to him your labour?
39.12: Do you trust in him That he does bring back your seed? And to your threshing-floor does gather it?
39.13: The wing of the rattling ones exults, Whether the pinion of the ostrich or hawk.
39.14: For she leaves on the earth her eggs, And on the dust she does warm them,
39.15: And she forgets that a foot may press it, And a beast of the field tread it down.
39.16: Her young ones it has hardened without her, In vain is her labour without fear.
39.17: For God has caused her to forget wisdom, And He has not given a portion To her in understanding:
39.18: At the time on high she lifts herself up, She laughs at the horse and at his rider.
39.19: Do you give to the horse might? Do you clothe his neck with a mane?
39.20: Do you cause him to rush as a locust? The majesty of his snorting is terrible.
39.21: They dig in a valley, and he rejoices in power, He goes forth to meet the armour.
39.22: He laughs at fear, and is not affrighted, And he turns not back from the face of the sword.
39.23: Against him rattle does quiver, The flame of a spear, and a halbert.
39.24: With trembling and rage he swallows the ground, And remains not stedfast Because of the sound of a trumpet.
39.25: Among the trumpets he says, Aha, And from afar he does smell battle, Roaring of princes and shouting.
39.26: By your understanding flies a hawk? Spreads he his wings to the south?
39.27: At your command goes an eagle up high? Or lifts he up his nest?
39.28: A rock he does inhabit, Yes, he lodges on the tooth of a rock, and fortress.
39.29: From from there he has sought food, To a far off place his eyes look attentively,
39.30: And his brood gulp up blood, And where the pierced are --there is he!

40.1: And Jehovah does answer Job, and says: --
40.2: Is the striver with the Mighty instructed? The reprover of God, let him answer it.
40.3: And Job answers Jehovah, and says: --
40.4: Indeed, I have been vile, What do I return to You? My hand I have placed on my mouth.
40.5: Once I have spoken, and I answer not, And twice, and I add not.
40.6: And Jehovah answers Job out of the whirlwind, and says: --
40.7: Gird, I pray you, as a man, your loins, I ask you, and cause you Me to know.
40.8: Do you also make void My judgment? Do you condemn Me, That you may be righteous?
40.9: And an arm like God have you? And with a voice like Him do you thunder?
40.10: Put on, I pray you, excellency and loftiness, Yes, honour and beauty put on.
40.11: Scatter abroad the wrath of your anger, And see every proud one, and make him low.
40.12: See every proud one--humble him, And tread down the wicked in their place.
40.13: Hide them in the dust together, Their faces bind in secret.
40.14: And even I--I do praise you, For your right hand gives salvation to you.
40.15: Indeed, I pray you, Behemoth, that I made with you: Grass as an ox he eats.
40.16: Indeed, I pray you, his power is in his loins, And his strength in the muscles of his belly.
40.17: He does bend his tail as a cedar, The sinews of his thighs are wrapped together,
40.18: His bones are tubes of brass, His bones are as a bar of iron.
40.19: He is a beginning of the ways of God, His Maker brings nigh his sword;
40.20: For food do mountains bear for him, And all the beasts of the field play there.
40.21: Under shades he lies down, In a secret place of reed and mire.
40.22: Cover him do shades, with their shadow, Cover him do willows of the brook.
40.23: Indeed, a flood oppresses--he does not haste, He is confident though Jordan Does come forth to his mouth.
40.24: Before his eyes does one take him, With snares does one pierce the nose?

41.1: Do you draw leviathan with an angle? And with a rope you let down--his tongue?
41.2: Do you put a reed in his nose? And with a thorn pierce his jaw?
41.3: Does he multiply to you supplications? Does he speak to you tender things?
41.4: Does he make a covenant with you? Do you take him for a servant age-during?
41.5: Do you play with him as a bird? And do you bind him for your damsels?
41.6: (Feast upon him do companions, They divide him among the merchants!)
41.7: Do you fill with barbed irons his skin? And with fish-spears his head?
41.8: Place on him your hand, Remember the battle--do not add!
41.9: Indeed, the hope of him is found a liar, Also at his appearance is not one cast down?
41.10: None so fierce that he does awake him, And who is he before Me stations himself?
41.11: Who has brought before Me and I repay? Under the whole heavens it is mine.
41.12: I do not keep silent concerning his parts, And the matter of might, And the grace of his arrangement.
41.13: Who has uncovered the face of his clothing? Within his double bridle who does enter?
41.14: The doors of his face who has opened? Round about his teeth are terrible.
41.15: A pride--strong ones of shields, Shut up--a close seal.
41.16: One to another they draw nigh, And air does not enter between them.
41.17: One to another they adhere, They stick together and are not separated.
41.18: His sneezings cause light to shine, And his eyes are as the eyelids of the dawn.
41.19: Out of his mouth do flames go, sparks of fire escape.
41.20: Out of his nostrils goes forth smoke, As a blown pot and reeds.
41.21: His breath sets coals on fire, And a flame from his mouth goes forth.
41.22: In his neck lodge does strength, And before him does grief exult.
41.23: The flakes of his flesh have adhered--Firm upon him--it is not moved.
41.24: His heart is firm as a stone, Yes, firm as the lower piece.
41.25: From his rising are the mighty afraid, From breakings they keep themselves free.
41.26: The sword of his overtaker stands not, Spear--dart--and lance.
41.27: He reckons iron as straw, brass as rotten wood.
41.28: The son of the bow does not cause him to flee, Turned by him into stubble are stones of the sling.
41.29: As stubble have darts been reckoned, And he laughs at the shaking of a javelin.
41.30: Under him are sharp points of clay, He spreads gold on the mire.
41.31: He causes to boil as a pot the deep, The sea he makes as a pot of ointment.
41.32: After him he causes a path to shine, One thinks the deep to be hoary.
41.33: There is not on the earth his like, That is made without terror.
41.34: Every high thing he does see, He is king over all sons of pride.

42.1: And Job answers Jehovah and says: --
42.2: You have known that for all things You are able, And not withheld from You is any device:
42.3: `Who is this, hiding counsel without knowledge?' Therefore, I have declared, and understand not, Too wonderful for me, and I know not.
42.4: `Hear, I pray you, and I--I do speak, I ask you, and cause you me to know.'
42.5: By the hearing of the ear I heard You, And now my eye has seen You.
42.6: Therefore do I loathe it, And I have repented on dust and ashes.
42.7: And it comes to pass after Jehovah's speaking these words to Job, that Jehovah says to Eliphaz the Temanite, `Burned has My anger against you, and against your two friends, because you have not spoken concerning Me rightly, like My servant Job.
42.8: And now, take to you seven bullocks and seven rams, and go you to My servant Job, and you have caused a burnt-offering to ascend for you; and Job My servant does pray for you, for surely his face I accept, so as not to do with you folly, because you have not spoken concerning Me rightly, like My servant Job.
42.9: And they go--Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, Zophar the Naamathite--and do as Jehovah has spoken to them; and Jehovah does accept the face of Job.
42.10: And Jehovah has turned to the captivity of Job in his praying for his friends, and Jehovah does add to all that Job has--to double.
42.11: And come to him do all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all his former acquaintances, and they eat bread with him in his house, and bemoan him, and comfort him concerning all the evil that Jehovah had brought upon him, and they gave to him each one kesitah, and each one ring of gold.
42.12: And Jehovah has blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning, and he has fourteen thousand of a flock, and six thousand camels, and a thousand pairs of oxen, and a thousand she-asses.
42.13: And he has seven sons and three daughters;
42.14: and he calls the name of the one Jemima, and the name of the second Kezia, and the name of the third Keren-Happuch.
42.15: And there have not been found women fair as the daughters of Job in all the land, and their father does give to them an inheritance in the midst of their brethren.
42.16: And Job lives after this a hundred and forty years, and sees his sons, and his sons' sons, four generations;
42.17: and Job dies, aged and satisfied with days.
